svg.title: How blurrd works
svg.desc: Architecture of blurrd. The desktop app and the command-line tool call the same engine jobs. Analysis: blurrd-video probes the recording and builds the timestamp table, blurrd-detect calibrates the HUD layout from sampled keyframes, one decoder (NVDEC, D3D11VA or software) feeds two to six crop and detect workers and one thread of temporal models, which turn the detections into box tracks. Verification: up to four OCR readers (PP-OCRv5 on ONNX Runtime with DirectML or the CPU) read the protected zones during the analysis; afterwards uncovered name parts are blurred in memory and read again, and readable names get OcrFix boxes, up to three rounds. Render: a second decoder trails the analysis, blurrd-blur blurs the YUV planes inside the boxes, NVENC, AMF, Quick Sync or Media Foundation encode, the muxer copies audio, and the export keeps the source name once verified or is marked UNVERIFIED. Measured on an RTX 4080 SUPER: about 10 seconds for a 60-second 1080p60 recording. Everything runs locally.
